panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Caption explicitly attributes case to hypochondroplasia with AP chest/pelvis showing narrowed sacrosciatic notch, a specific hypochondroplasia pelvic finding. B: Hypochondroplasia case, AP legs panel. In-text documents rhizomelic shortening; caption notes distal fibular overgrowth proposed as additional finding. C: Hypochondroplasia case, AP arm with captioned mild rhizomelic shortening, matching shortened long bones vocabulary. D: Hypochondroplasia case, lateral lumbar spine with captioned narrowed spinal canal supporting caudal narrowing/stenosis finding; platyspondyly not in vocabulary proposed. E: Hypochondroplasia case, PA left hand age 5 with captioned brachydactyly, direct vocabulary match. F: Hypochondroplasia case, PA left hand age 12.5 with captioned brachymetacarpia indicating short-hand phenotype, vocabulary brachydactyly match.
panels.attribution_text: Xue et al. FGFR3 mutation frequency in 324 cases from the International Skeletal Dysplasia Registry.. Molecular genetics & genomic medicine 2014. doi:10.1002/mgg3.96. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Radiographs of a case of hypochondroplasia with a p.Gly380Arg mutation (R# 92-231A). (A) AP chest and pelvis, age 5 years. The sacrosciatic notch is narrowed, but there is no interpediculate narrowing. (B) AP legs, age 5 years. There is distal fibular overgrowth. (C) AP arm, age 5 years. There is only mild rhizomelic shortening. (D) Lateral lumbar spine, age 12.5 years. There is mild platyspondyly and a narrowed spinal canal. (E) PA left hand, age 5 years. Note the brachydactyly and brachymetacarpia. (F) PA, left hand, age 12.5 years. The brachymetacarpia is less pronounced than at age 5.
in_text_mentions: In Figure2, milder radiographic findings such as mild interpediculate narrowing suggest a diagnosis of HCH although this patient (R#92-231A) had a p.Gly380Arg mutation. He was born at term and his growth was in the normal range until age 2. The paternal height was 188 cm and the maternal height was 163 cm. At age 6 years 9 months, he began being followed by an endocrinologist. His height was 105.8 cm (+2.5 SD on the ACH chart). Radiographs of ilias revealed short iliac bones

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Front view clinical photo of 7yr 8mo proband with disproportionate short-limbed dwarfism consistent with hypochondroplasia clinico-radiologic criteria per article. B: Lateral lumbar spine radiograph of same proband showing caudal narrowing of interpediculate distance, classic HCH radiologic sign. C: AP pelvis radiograph of same proband showing short iliac bones and short femoral necks consistent with HCH pelvis phenotype.
panels.attribution_text: Yao et al. Identification of a novel mutation of FGFR3 gene in a large Chinese pedigree with hypochondroplasia by next-generation sequencing: A case report and brief literature review.. Medicine 2019. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000014157. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical and radiologic findings of the proband at the age of 7 yr and 8 mo. A. Front view illustrated a disproportionate dwarf with normal face. B. Radiographs of front spine showed that interpedicular distance was slightly smaller at L-5 than at L-1. C. Radiographs of ilias revealed short iliac bones and short femoral necks.
in_text_mentions: The proband was a disproportionate dwarf with short-limbs, brachydactyly and slight genu varum (Fig. 2A) but she did not have trident hands. Her face is normal and she is of normal intelligence. Current weight was 23.1 kg (–0.3 SD), height 116.0 cm (–2.1 SD), her upper to lower segment ratio 1.32 and head circumference 52.2 cm. Her serum concentrations of alkaline phosphatase, insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), IGF-binding proteins, and thyroid hormone were normal.

Radiological studies revealed short limbs with slight brachydactyly, caudad narrowing of the interpediculate distance of the lumbar spine (Fig. 2B), short iliac bones and short femoral necks (Fig. 2C), short stubby tibias, mildly increased fibular lengths and genu varum. Her clinical and radiologic findings were consistent with clinico-radiologic criteria for HCH.[8]
